findings.claim: In `test_state_results_multi_group`, the expected occurrence for `group_2` is built with `value=6`, while the data packet has `group_2=10`. The test passes only because the value is not used when the occurrence is constructed.

verifier.reason: In tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:177, `test_state_results_multi_group` sets `"group_2": 10` in `data_packet`, yet builds `occurrence_2` with `value=6` at lines 190-192. The test still passes because `build_mock_occurrence_and_event` (lines 244-275) never uses its `value` parameter when constructing `occurrence` or `event_data` (and `IssueOccurrence.__eq__` in src/sentry/issues/issue_occurrence.py:180-183 compares only `id`).

findings.claim: The Kafka publish assertion allows extra publishes, so the test does not catch duplicate occurrence production.

verifier.reason: In tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:206-222, test_state_results_multi_group only calls mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.assert_has_calls([...], any_order=True) without checking mock_produce_occurrence_to_kafka.call_count == 2. Because unittest.mock's assert_has_calls only verifies that the expected calls appear as a subset of mock_calls, extra or duplicate Kafka occurrence publishes would pass undetected.
